title: Modbus Device Communication Failure Rate
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Modbus Device Communication Failure Rate' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_modbus_device_communication_failure_rate` (UC-14.1.8), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — Modbus Device Communication Failure Rate", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=ot` sourcetype='modbus:poll_log' that satisfy the UC-14.1.8 SPL filters for 'Modbus Device Communication Failure Rate'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `ot` / `modbus:poll_log` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `operational_exceptions.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-14.1.8.

dataSources: Modbus gateway/master logs (poll success/failure per slave address) Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Splunk Edge Hub, custom (Modbus polling logs) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=ot sourcetype="modbus:poll_log" OR sourcetype="modbus:gateway"
| rex "slave=(?<slave_addr>\d+)|address=(?<slave_addr>\d+)|(?<status>success|timeout|failure|error)"
| eval poll_ok=if(lower(status)="success", 1, 0), poll_fail=if(lower(status)!="success" AND status!="", 1, 0)
| bin _time span=15m
| stats sum(poll_ok) as ok, sum(poll_fail) as fail by slave_addr, host, _time
| eval total=ok+fail, failure_rate_pct=if(total>0, (fail/total)*100, 0)
| where failure_rate_pct > 10 OR fail > 5
| table slave_addr, host, ok, fail, failure_rate_pct
description: Poll timeout tracking across Modbus TCP/RTU slaves identifies communication failures before they impact process control. High failure rates indicate network issues, slave overload, or misconfiguration.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Edge Hub, custom (Modbus polling logs).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: Modbus gateway/master logs (poll success/failure per slave address).
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure Modbus gateway or Edge Hub Modbus connector to log poll success/failure per slave address. Parse slave address and status from logs. Ingest via syslog or file monitor. Alert when failure rate exceeds 10% over 15 minutes or more than 5 consecutive failures for a critical slave. Correlate with network and PLC health.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=ot sourcetype="modbus:poll_log" OR sourcetype="modbus:gateway"
| rex "slave=(?<slave_addr>\d+)|address=(?<slave_addr>\d+)|(?<status>success|timeout|failure|error)"
| eval poll_ok=if(lower(status)="success", 1, 0), poll_fail=if(lower(status)!="success" AND status!="", 1, 0)
| bin _time span=15m
| stats sum(poll_ok) as ok, sum(poll_fail) as fail by slave_addr, host, _time
| eval total=ok+fail, failure_rate_pct=if(total>0, (fail/total)*100, 0)
| where failure_rate_pct > 10 OR fail > 5
| table slave_addr, host, ok, fail, failure_rate_pct
```

Understanding this SPL

**Modbus Device Communication Failure Rate** — Poll timeout tracking across Modbus TCP/RTU slaves identifies communication failures before they impact process control. High failure rates indicate network issues, slave overload, or misconfiguration.

Documented **Data sources**: Modbus gateway/master logs (poll success/failure per slave address). **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Edge Hub, custom (Modbus polling logs). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: ot; **sourcetype**: modbus:poll_log, modbus:gateway. If that sourcetype is not mentioned in Data sources, double-check parsing or update the documentation to match the feed you actually ingest.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=ot, sourcetype="modbus:poll_log". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• Extracts fields with `rex` (regular expression).
• `eval` defines or adjusts **poll_ok** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Discretizes time or numeric ranges with `bin`/`bucket`.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by slave_addr, host, _time** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **total** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Filters the current rows with `where failure_rate_pct > 10 OR fail > 5` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.
• Pipeline stage (see **Modbus Device Communication Failure Rate**): table slave_addr, host, ok, fail, failure_rate_pct


Step 3 — Validate
Run the search in a known window. Spot-check a few events against the BMS console (for example Niagara, Tridium, or Honeywell) and confirm zones, values, and alarms line up. Verify field names and that the right roles can search the index.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Table (slaves with high failure rate), Line chart (failure rate trend by slave), Bar chart (top failing slaves), Single value (slaves in spec %).
